title: Please Get Me Out of My Own Drawing — Playable Storytime

direction.promise: The eraser is removing the drawn ground. Help Nemi reach the same real desk outside the book.
direction.want: She wants the ordinary solid desk beyond the page.
direction.choice: Keep following one physical escape route; inspect the next obstruction and choose an action.
direction.consequence: Ink shortcuts vanish; real paper holds; the same solid eraser carries her over the ink it removes.
direction.payoff: She gets off the drawing onto the real desk, where she is safe from being rubbed out.

chapters.name: Get me off the page
chapters.framing: Continue the same escape with a stable actor, floor and material landmark.

lines.text: I drew this place, and that eraser is eating the floor. I'm on that floor. Click and drag to look around, or swipe on your phone. Find the door to your left or the tear to your right, then press one for the door, or two for the tear.
On phones, tap the matching chapter. You can pause to look.

lines.text: Oh, of course. It's a drawing of a door. I gave it a doorknob and absolutely no depth.
The little keyhole was ambitious. Let's put that back. Try two for the tear; I can be embarrassed somewhere with an actual opening.
That eraser is still coming. Keep going.

lines.text: Wait, there's actual space behind the paper. We can get through that! My best exit is the bit I didn't draw.
And there's my real desk beyond it. Once I'm on that desk, I'm outside the drawing, where the eraser can't reach me. But there's a gap before I get there.

lines.text: Oh. I stopped drawing the bridge halfway across. Apparently I thought Future Me would deal with it. Look underneath the left route, then at that loose paper tab on the right. Four to run across, or five to fold the tab.

lines.text: I was going to take a very confident first step. The bridge has taken it for me. Right into the hole. That's useful information to get before the rest of me follows. Back it up. Five for the paper tab, please.
We still need that desk. The eraser hasn't stopped, and neither can we.

lines.text: There, that fold reaches the other side, and the crease is holding. Okay, small steps. I'm trusting paper with my entire existence, which feels like a fairly normal day in animation. There, both feet are across. I think I'm allowed to breathe now.

chapters.name: The eraser is going there
chapters.framing: Continue the same escape with a stable actor, floor and material landmark.

lines.text: Look to our right. It's the same eraser, still heading toward my desk and wiping out the ink path. The ground won't last much longer. But that solid top isn't made of ink, so we could use it as a lift. Seven to race it, or eight to ride it straight onto that desk.

Straight onto the desk. Then we're off the page.
